assertion: Forty-six percent of U.S. adults say crime has increased nationally over the past year, down sharply from 77% in 2023 and little changed from 49% last year. The figure has been lower only once since Gallup began tracking national perceptions in 1989.
independent_value: Gallup: 46%, 49% last year, 77% three years ago; lower only in 2001 (41%). R Street repeats it.

assertion: About a third, 33%, say local crime has increased over the past year, among the lowest readings in more than five decades of polling.
independent_value: Gallup: 33%; lower only three times (31% 1998, 26% 2001, 30% last year)

assertion: In 2022, a record 56% of Americans said crime was rising locally, compared with 33% today.
independent_value: Gallup: 56% in 2022 was the most negative local reading

assertion: Republicans' perceptions of rising national crime fell another 15 percentage points in the latest survey.
independent_value: Gallup: fell another 15 points; Democrats and independents steady

assertion: Seven in 10 Americans say they worry at least occasionally about becoming victims of identity theft, while 55% worry about being tricked by scammers into sending money or providing access to their financial accounts. Those were the only two offenses among 10 surveyed that worried a majority of respondents.
measure: Gallup poll worry identity theft scams

assertion: By comparison, 41% worry about having their vehicle stolen or broken into, while the same share worry about a school-age child being physically harmed at school. About 37% fear a home burglary, and 22% worry about being murdered.

Among adults 55 and older, 77% express concern about identity theft, compared with 52% of adults younger than 35. Nearly a third of adults earning less than $50,000 annually worry about being murdered, compared with 13% of those earning at least $100,000. Sexual assault worries 40% of women compared with 13% of men.
Violent crime fell 9.3% in 2025 from the previous year, the largest annual drop since the agency began tracking national estimates in 1936.
warehouse_value: crime.cde_offenses violent-crime rate monthly average 30.32 (2024) to 27.34 (2025) = -9.8% (rough proxy)
sql: SELECT "year", offense_code, AVG(national_offense_rate) FROM crime.cde_offenses WHERE offense_code IN ('homicide','violent-crime') AND "year" IN (2023,2024,2025) GROUP BY "year", offense_code
independent_value: Register-Herald copy of Stateline story, Gallup and R Street state 9.3% and largest since 1936

assertion: The murder rate also plunged 18.5% to 4.1 killings per 100,000 people, tying its lowest recorded level in nearly 90 years. The rate matches those recorded in 1955 and 1956.
inaccuracy: The percentage is 18.1% in the Stateline-originated copy; 18.5% is the FBI robbery decline. Warehouse proxy shows -18.0%. The 4.1 rate and 1955/1956 tie match.
sql: SELECT "year", offense_code, AVG(national_offense_rate) FROM crime.cde_offenses WHERE offense_code='homicide' GROUP BY "year"
independent_value: Register-Herald copy: murder rate fell 18.1% to 4.1, matches 1955 and 1956; robbery fell 18.5%

assertion: Preliminary findings from the federal Bureau of Justice Statistics' National Crime Victimization Survey, which captures nonfatal crimes whether or not they were reported to law enforcement, showed that violent victimization, excluding simple assault, fell 25% in 2025. Aggravated assaults dropped 31%, while robberies declined 27%.
independent_value: CBS News on BJS release: about 25% drop excl. simple assault; aggravated assault 31%; robbery 27%. KCCI: 25% drop excluding simple assault. Warehouse NCVS loaded only through 2024.

assertion: Americans are increasingly optimistic about the nation's crime trends, with perceptions of rising crime hovering near historic lows even as nearly half the country still believes crime is getting worse.
inaccuracy: Level near lowest since 2001, but the 49% to 46% change is within the +/-4 margin and the article itself says 'little changed'; 'increasingly' overstates the one-year move
independent_value: Gallup: 'little changed' from 49%; 'most positive in 25 years'
